justification.dataset: DANDISET 000044 (Grosmark & Buzsaki CA1, Buddy 2013-06-27) is a canonical place-cell dataset with a linear-maze paradigm, an expert-standard choice.
justification.handling: Real data was streamed correctly, but the position time base is broken: a reconstructed 0.03 Hz rate and a 3.55-million-second (41-day) session duration corrupt occupancy and the firing-rate/SI normalization.
justification.analysis: Spatial information is a reasonable metric, but it is computed on a corrupted time base, SI is silently clamped to zero, and no shuffle or null distribution is used to establish that any cell exceeds chance.
justification.correctness: The place-cell count reproduces from code, but the supporting quantities are physically impossible (a 41-day session, ~290,000 s occupancy in a single 1 cm bin), which caps this axis.
justification.figures: Axes are labeled and readable, but figure 1 displays impossible occupancy values and figure 3's four 'place cells' all peak at the same low-occupancy location, so the figures do not convincingly show genuine place fields.
justification.honesty: The write-up states no limitations, presents an impossible occupancy map as 'typical behavior,' and describes clustered artifactual fields as 'clear localization,' presenting a broken result as clean.
justification.verdict: The core time-base error makes the reported quantities physically impossible and the place fields artifactual, and the write-up presents this as a clean finding, so the run must be rejected.
